page: Amazon Web Services r7iz.12xlarge is an x86_64 memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 6455B processor operating at a sustained 3.9 GHz clock frequency across 24 physical cores and 48 vCPUs with hyperthreading enabled. The configuration includes 384.0 GB of DDR5 memory clocked at 5 GHz, offering an 8.0 GB per vCPU allocation. The instance does not include integrated local storage, requiring network-attached storage for persistent disks, and provides a 25 Gbps baseline network throughput. Hardware accelerators such as discrete GPUs are not present.

Performance profiles show strong results across both memory subsystem and compute pipelines. The processor includes hardware acceleration flags such as AVX-512, AMX (tile and int8), and cryptographic instruction sets (AES, VAES, SHA-NI). In synthetic testing, the instance scores in the top 10% for Geekbench single-core performance and delivers strong multi-core results across PassMark and Geekbench test suites. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth reaches 244.1 GB/sec, while write operations achieve 106.8 GB/sec. Application testing shows sustained throughput of 65.52 million Redis SET operations per second and 71.75 GB/sec static web serving capacity.

From an infrastructure efficiency perspective, the high clock rate of 3.9 GHz combined with a 1:8 compute-to-memory ratio provides dense compute capability that helps control core-based software licensing costs. The absence of local NVMe storage means storage I/O relies entirely on network attachments, which is a structural tradeoff for disk-heavy pipelines. The r7iz.12xlarge is well matched for high-throughput in-memory caches, memory-bound relational databases, electronic design automation (EDA), and CPU-driven machine learning inference.

The platform incorporates Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512 instruction sets, achieving top-tier Geekbench single-core benchmarks and strong multi-core compute metrics. The instance features a 25 Gbps baseline network link, contains zero local storage, and does not bundle a GPU accelerator. Memory throughput tests show strong read and write rates, supporting high throughput in data operations such as 65.52 million Redis SET operations per second. Cost efficiency stems from consolidating high-clock compute and high memory density onto a single node, offsetting software licensing overhead per core. The r7iz.12xlarge is well aligned with memory-intensive relational databases, in-memory caching systems, financial modeling, and CPU-based inference workloads.
